title: Technique for Liquid Culture of Early Chick Embryos Suitable for Long Term Live Imaging
protocol: Prepare 0.6% Bacto agar in 121 mM NaCl.
Cool to 48°C in a water bath.
Mix 50 ml of thin albumin collected from fertilized eggs with the cooled agar solution.
Pour 3 ml of the mixture into culture plates and allow to gel at room temperature.
Sterilize circular rings of Whatman filter paper by cutting out the central disk (25 mm).
Break eggs in a clean 10 cm petri dish, keeping the vitelline membrane intact around the yolk.
Orient the yolk so that the embryo is on top.
Clean the surface of the vitelline membrane with sterile tissue.
Place the filter paper ring on top of the vitelline membrane to center the embryo in the hole.
Cut the vitelline membrane around the outer edges of the filtering with small scissors.
Gently lift the embryo off the yolk using fine forceps.
Place the embryos with the epiblast side down onto the agar albumin-filled culture dish.
Position the dish under a dissecting microscope.
Remove excess yolk from the embryos with fine tweezers.
Sterilize the culture plates with 70% ethanol.
Rinse the sterilized plates with sterile distilled water.
Fill central depression of culture plate with 30 μl of heavy Silicon oil.
Take the filter paper mounted embryo from the culture plate and place it hypoblast side down over the central depression of the culture plate.
Place rubber O ring in the groove of the culture plate and press down gently with the help of two forceps.
Remove the filter ring outside the embryo by tearing the vitelline membrane with fine forces.
Place the culture plate in a sterile 3cm petri dish and fill it with 3 ml of thin albumin, removing any yolk extruding from under the vitelline membrane into the four escape ports.
Mount the culture plate at the bottom of an observation chamber for lightsheet microscope observation.
Prepare an agar mould that fits the culture plate by placing an unused culture plate in the centre of the observation chamber and filling it with 2 ml of 1% agar in saline.
Replace the empty culture plate with the culture plate containing the embryo once the agar is solidified.
Fill the box with 10 ml of thin egg white, optionally including Pen/Strep to prevent bacterial contamination.
Mount preparation under the Lightsheet microscope.
Cover the albumin with 2 ml light silicon oil to prevent evaporation.
